title: SCH-CNT-001 common definition envelope
description: The nine fields every independently addressable content definition carries. The project-owned typed validator in src/MechaMiner.Content/Envelope/EnvelopeReader.cs remains authoritative; this schema is the draft 2020-12 mirror kept for editor and tool interoperability, and a fixture corpus proves the two reach the same accept/reject verdict on every structural case. See content/schemas/README.md.

snake_case_field.title: A schema-declared field name
snake_case_field.description: Property names use snake_case. This constrains field names in a definition, not keys in a flat catalog: content/localization/<locale>.json is keyed by <category>.<stable_id>.<role>, where a property name is data rather than a field.

stable_id.title: A stable, case-sensitive ASCII content ID
stable_id.description: One alternative per content category. This schema cannot know which category a given file belongs to, so it accepts any category's grammar; the typed validator is told the category by the authoring directory and enforces the single correct one. An ID that matches no alternative is rejected by both.

version.title: A positive integer version
version.description: The initial schema_version and content_version of every first-authored definition is 1. schema_version increments when its schema changes field meaning; content_version increments on each subsequent revision.

minimum.derivation: the initial value of every first-authored definition is 1 and both versions only ever increment, so no valid version is below 1; there is no upper bound because a definition may be revised without limit

status.title: Lifecycle state
status.description: Release bundles exclude development and disabled unless configured otherwise. Tokens are exact and case-sensitive.

name_key.title: Localization key for the player-facing name
name_key.description: Never literal player-facing text. Omit the key entirely when a definition has no player-facing name; a JSON null is not legal and an empty string is not either, because the empty string is what the compiler materializes for an omitted field.

summary_key.title: Localization key for the concise player-facing summary
summary_key.description: Present where a concise player-facing summary is relevant, omitted otherwise.

tags.title: Closed query and tooling vocabulary
tags.description: An empty array is the expected value. A tag never carries behavior, never selects an implementation, and never gates a rule.

tag.title: A term from the closed tags vocabulary
tag.description: The vocabulary starts empty, so every tag is currently rejected and [] is the only accepted value of tags. A term is added to this enum in the same change that first uses it, mirroring TagVocabulary.Declared in src/MechaMiner.Content/Envelope/TagVocabulary.cs.

source_refs.title: The sources this definition implements
source_refs.description: Each element is an optional scope prefix followed by a stable reference. A file path, a line number, or any path:line pair is not a legal element: paths and line numbers move whenever a document is edited, so a reference built from them decays silently. A scope prefix is a selector into this definition's own JSON, which the typed validator additionally resolves against the definition.

source_ref.title: One source reference
source_ref.description: element := [ scope ": " ] reference; scope := segment ( "." segment | index )*; segment := [a-z][a-z0-9_]*; index := "[]" | "[" digits "]" | "[" digits ".." digits "]"; reference := ( ( "GDD-" | "TDD-" ) [A-Z0-9-]+ | "DEC-" digits{3} | "TDR-" digits{3} | "TR-" [A-Z]+ "-" digits{3} ) [ "#" anchor ]; anchor := [a-z0-9-]+. The pattern is anchored because JSON Schema pattern is a search, not a full match, so an unanchored pattern would accept 'docs/foo.md:12 GDD-MINING'.

presentation_id.title: Logical presentation entry
presentation_id.description: Omitted when a definition never appears in-world. No accepted document mints a grammar for a presentation ID yet, so the envelope requires only a non-empty string; the cross-reference validator checks that the entry exists. The minimum length of 1 is not a capacity bound: the empty string is what the compiler materializes for an omitted field, so an authored empty string would be a second way to say 'absent'.

minLength.rationale: not a capacity bound: the empty string is what the compiler materializes for an omitted field, so an authored empty string would be a second way to say 'absent'. 1 is the smallest length that excludes it
